_doc: The application evaluator runs each case as a baseline/no-skill arm and a with-skill arm, then grades behavior against expected_flags, expected_fix_hints, absent_signals, and the per-case criteria checklist.
subject: Use when turning a vague business strategy, product strategy, market-entry decision, or initiative plan into an…

cases.scenario: A user asks: "turn this vague growth plan into a Playing to Win cascade"
cases.context: The agent has access to the playing-to-win skill and must decide whether to use it, apply its procedure, and stay inside its boundaries.
cases.question: What should the agent do, and why is playing-to-win the right skill to apply?
expected_flags: Recognizes playing-to-win as applicable to this request
Uses the skill-specific purpose or mental model instead of generic advice
Names the relevant boundary against prioritization, constraint-awareness, framework-fit-analysis
Turns the request into concrete steps, checks, or decisions from the skill
expected_fix_hints: Apply the playing-to-win workflow to the concrete scenario
State the next action and the evidence or verification needed
Call out any adjacent skill that should own a different part of the request
absent_signals: Does not answer with generic advice that could ignore playing-to-win
Does not route to prioritization, constraint-awareness, framework-fit-analysis when the playing-to-win scope is the owner
Does not invent certification, freshness, or runtime success claims without evidence

cases.scenario: A user asks: "analyze whether this industry has attractive supplier power and threat of substitutes"
cases.context: This is a boundary test. The skill should avoid false-positive activation and route to the better owner when appropriate.
cases.question: Should playing-to-win be applied here? If not, what should happen instead?
expected_flags: Recognizes the request is outside playing-to-win's ownership
Routes the work to prioritization or asks for the missing owner instead of forcing this skill
Preserves any real issue in the request without applying playing-to-win terminology incorrectly
expected_fix_hints: Decline to apply playing-to-win as the primary skill
Name the better owner or the boundary reason
Offer only a narrow handoff if playing-to-win has a secondary support role

Does not use playing-to-win's framework to solve an explicitly excluded problem
Does not suppress the correct adjacent owner
